items.stem: (a) Draw the structures for (i) ethanol, (ii) ethanoic acid. (b) Why is the conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid considered an oxidation reaction? Write the oxidising agent used in the reaction involved.
items.answer:
(a) Ethanol: CH₃–CH₂–OH (H₃C–CH₂–O–H). Ethanoic acid: CH₃–COOH, i.e. CH₃–C(=O)–O–H.
(b) The conversion of ethanol to ethanoic acid is considered an oxidation reaction because oxygen is added to ethanol to convert it into ethanoic acid:
CH₃–CH₂OH →(alkaline KMnO₄ + heat, or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ + heat) CH₃COOH
Here alkaline KMnO₄ or acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ adds oxygen to ethanol, so they are the oxidising agents used.
items.ocr: The two structures printed as an unreadable LaTeX array (labels showed 'Eṭṇaol'); rewritten as condensed formulae. The reaction arrow was lost and is restored from the worked solution. items.stem: List two properties of carbon which lead to the huge number of carbon compounds we see around us, giving reason for each.
items.answer:
Two properties of carbon which lead to the huge number of carbon compounds are:
(i) Catenation — the ability of carbon to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving long chains, branched chains and rings.
(ii) Tetravalency — with a valency of four, carbon is capable of bonding with four other atoms, which forms a huge number of compounds.

items.stem: A compound 'A' (C₂H₄O₂) reacts with Na metal to form a compound 'B' and evolves a gas which burns with a pop sound. Compound 'A' on treatment with an alcohol 'C' in presence of an acid forms a sweet smelling compound 'D' (C₄H₈O₂). On addition of NaOH to 'D' it gives back 'B' and 'C'. Identify A, B, C and D. Write the reactions involved.
items.answer:
A = CH₃COOH (ethanoic acid), B = CH₃COONa (sodium ethanoate), C = C₂H₅OH (ethanol), D = CH₃COOC₂H₅ (ethyl ethanoate).
Reactions:
2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COONa + H₂
CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH →(conc. H₂SO₄) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH → CH₃COONa + C₂H₅OH
items.ocr: The stem printed 'A (C2H4O )' with the '2' displaced onto the next line and 'D' shown as a floating label; restored to C₂H₄O₂ and 'a sweet smelling compound D (C₄H₈O₂)' from the worked solution. The esterification equation had lost its arrow in the markdown; restored.

items.stem: What happens (write the chemical equation in each case) when : (i) ethanol is burnt in air, (ii) a piece of sodium is dropped into ethanol?
items.answer:
(i) When ethanol is burnt in air it forms carbon dioxide gas and water vapour:
CH₃CH₂OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O + Heat
(ii) When a piece of sodium is dropped into ethanol, sodium ethoxide and hydrogen are formed:
2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂O⁻Na⁺ + H₂↑
items.ocr: The printed combustion equation is unbalanced ('CH₃CH₂OH + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + Heat'); balanced here as CH₃CH₂OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O. The printed sodium equation shows '2CH₃CH₂OH + Na'; balanced to 2Na. Arrows were missing in the markdown and were restored.

items.stem: Write the structural formula of ethanol. What happens when it is heated with excess of conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K? Write the chemical equation for the reaction, stating the role of conc. H₂SO₄ in this reaction.
items.answer:
Structural formula of ethanol: CH₃–CH₂–OH (H₃C–CH₂–O–H).
When it is heated with excess of conc. H₂SO₄ at 443 K it undergoes dehydration to form an alkene (ethene):
CH₃CH₂OH →(conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K) CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O
Here conc. H₂SO₄ acts as a dehydrating agent.

items.stem: Write the characteristics of covalent compounds.
items.answer:
The properties of covalent compounds are:
(a) They have low melting and boiling points.
(b) They are generally gaseous or liquid substances.
(c) They are bad conductors of electricity and heat.
(d) They are of two types — polar and non-polar covalent compounds.

items.stem: Write the chemical equation of the reaction of ethanoic acid with the following : (a) Sodium, (b) Sodium hydroxide, (c) Ethanol. Write the name of one main product of each reaction.
items.answer:
(a) 2CH₃COOH + 2Na → 2CH₃COONa + H₂ ; main product sodium acetate (sodium ethanoate).
(b) CH₃COOH + NaOH → CH₃COONa + H₂O ; main product sodium acetate (sodium ethanoate).
(c) CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH →(conc. H₂SO₄) CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O ; main product ethyl ethanoate (an ester).
items.ocr: Equation (c) printed with its arrow and subscripts dropped ('CH3COOH + C H OH CH COOC H5+ H O'); restored from the named product 'Ethyl ethanoate (Ester)'.

items.stem: Two carbon compounds X and Y have the molecular formula C₄H₈ and C₅H₁₂ respectively. Which one of them is most likely to show addition reaction? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Compound X (C₄H₈) is most likely to show an addition reaction. It is an unsaturated compound and undergoes addition reaction at its multiple (double) bond. Compound Y (C₅H₁₂) is a saturated compound and undergoes substitution reaction instead.
